mil3.3.5:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, are there any formations that come to be without having existed?”
mil3.3.5:1.3: “There are no formations, Great King, that come to be without having existed; it is only formations that already exist, Great King, that come to be.”
mil3.3.5:2.2: “What do you think, Great King: did this house in which you are sitting come to be without having existed?”
mil3.3.5:2.3: “Nothing here, venerable sir, has come to be without having existed; it has come to be only from what existed. These timbers, venerable sir, were in the forest, and this clay was in the earth; it was by the appropriate efforts of women and men that this house came to be.”
mil3.3.5:2.4: “In the same way, Great King, there are no formations that come to be without having existed; it is only formations that already exist that come to be.”
mil3.3.5:3.2: “Just as, Great King, all those kinds of seeds and plants that are planted in the ground and, in due course reaching growth, increase, and abundance, would give flowers and fruits—those trees did not come to be without having existed; those trees came to be only from what existed;
mil3.3.5:3.3: in the same way, Great King, there are no formations that come to be without having existed; it is only those formations that already exist that come to be.”
mil3.3.5:4.2: “Just as, Great King, a potter, having dug up clay from the earth, makes various vessels—those vessels did not come to be without having existed; they came to be only from what existed;
mil3.3.5:4.3: in the same way, Great King, there are no formations that come to be without having existed; it is only formations that already exist that come to be.”
mil3.3.5:5.2: “Suppose, Great King, a lute had no bowl, no skin, no frame, no neck, no bridge, no strings, no plectrum, and there were no appropriate effort of a man—would a sound arise?”
mil3.3.5:5.4: “But if, Great King, a lute had its bowl, its skin, its frame, its neck, its bridge, its strings, and its plectrum, and there were the appropriate effort of a man—would a sound arise?”
mil3.3.5:5.6: “In the same way, Great King, there are no formations that come to be without having existed; it is only formations that already exist that come to be.”
mil3.3.5:6.2: “Suppose, Great King, there were no fire-stick, no fire-stick base, no fire-stick cord, no upper fire-stick, no tinder cloth, and there were no appropriate effort of a man—would that fire arise?”
mil3.3.5:6.4: “But if, Great King, there were a fire-stick, a fire-stick base, a fire-stick cord, an upper fire-stick, a tinder cloth, and the appropriate effort of a man—would that fire arise?”
mil3.3.5:6.6: “In the same way, Great King, there are no formations that come to be without having existed; it is only formations that already exist that come to be.”
mil3.3.5:7.2: “Suppose, Great King, there were no crystal, no sunlight, and no cow dung—would that fire arise?”
mil3.3.5:7.4: “But if, Great King, there were a crystal, sunlight, and cow dung—would that fire arise?”
mil3.3.5:7.6: “In the same way, Great King, there are no formations that come to be without having existed; it is only formations that already exist that come to be.”
mil3.3.5:8.2: “Suppose, Great King, there were no mirror, no light, and no face—would a reflection of oneself arise?”
mil3.3.5:8.4: “But if, Great King, there were a mirror, light, and a face—would a reflection of oneself arise?”
mil3.3.5:8.6: “In the same way, Great King, there are no formations that come to be without having existed; it is only formations that already exist that come to be.”
